# Lyrion Music Server (`lms-community-slimserver`)

Experience the ultimate audio streaming solution with Lyrion Music Server. Effortlessly stream local and internet music to any device, transforming your listening experience across platforms like Windows, macOS, and Linux.

[Source](https://github.com/LMS-Community/slimserver)

## Example

```terraform
resource "osc_instance" "example" {
  service_id = "lms-community-slimserver"
  name       = "myslimserver"

  parameters = {
    # MusicBucketUrl    = "..."
    # S3EndpointUrl     = "..."
    # S3AccessKeyId     = "..."
    # S3SecretAccessKey = "..."
    # S3Region          = "..."
  }
}
```

Commented lines are optional parameters. Values marked `"..."` need a real value. Outputs are `url`, `external_ip`, `external_port` and the raw `instance` document, see the `osc_instance` resource.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `MusicBucketUrl` | string | no | Specifies the URL or path to a cloud storage bucket containing music files that the Lyrion Music Server should access and stream from |
| `S3EndpointUrl` | string | no | Sets the endpoint URL for S3-compatible storage services, allowing connection to custom S3 implementations or alternative cloud storage providers |
| `S3AccessKeyId` | string | no | Provides the access key ID for authenticating with AWS S3 or S3-compatible storage services to access music files stored in cloud buckets |
| `S3SecretAccessKey` | string | no | Provides the secret access key for authenticating with AWS S3 or S3-compatible storage services, paired with the access key ID for secure bucket access |
| `S3Region` | string | no | Specifies the AWS region where the S3 bucket containing music files is located, ensuring proper routing and compliance with data locality requirements |

The instance `name` must match `^\w+$` and be unique per service within the workspace. OSC lowercases it and allows at most 20 characters.

Parameter values are strings; booleans take `"true"` or `"false"`. Reference an `osc_secret` as `osc_secret.<name>.ref` to keep a value out of the instance configuration. This page is generated from the OSC catalog; the provider validates against the live catalog when planning.
